SMTO-LLM-0043 — The model's instructions for a tool couldn't be read

GUID: 49ab6448-b69a-40a2-a062-a33d5f9ad00b
Slug: invalid-tool-argument-object
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: llm

What happened

  • The model asked to use a tool, but the details it gave weren't one clear, readable set. SMTO didn't run that tool.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait to see whether the Run continues. SMTO may ask the model once more by itself after a reply it can't use. The model may send readable tool details on its next try.
  2. If the Run stopped, read its activity in the conversation to see which steps already finished, then ask the Agent to continue only the rest. The tool was not run, but steps before it already happened. Repeating them could do the same work twice.
  3. If it keeps happening, ask the person who runs the model server to check its tool-call settings for this model, or choose a different model in Settings › Setup › Model routing. Unreadable tool details usually come from how the model server formats tool requests.

What success looks like

  • The Run continues past this step, and the Agent's next action appears in its activity.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who runs the model server or manages SMTO. Don't ask the Agent to redo steps that already finished.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The tool call's arguments cannot be represented as one finite JSON object (non-object root, duplicate member, NaN/Infinity or overflowing number, or an unserializable value).

What this means

  • Tool arguments must encode one finite JSON object; non-object values, invalid numeric constants or unserializable members cannot represent a valid argument set. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Tool arguments must encode one finite JSON object; non-object values, invalid numeric constants or unserializable members cannot represent a valid argument set.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the argument representation and finite-number constraints against the advertised tool schema; do not execute a repaired guess.

How to fix it

  • Raised by argument_text and json_object in src/agent_runtime/llm/openai_compat/response.py. Inspect the call's raw arguments in the trace and fix the provider's tool-call parser or chat template so arguments are a single standard JSON object matching the tool's arguments schema; keep validation enabled.
  • Correct the provider/tool parser configuration and ensure arguments are a single object matching the advertised schema.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The arguments decode to one finite JSON object and pass the tool's schema checks.

What not to do

  • Do not replay prior successful operations to repair a later model response.
  • Do not disable protocol validation or treat this representation failure as input-context overflow.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
